title: Code refactor regression harness and prompt bank (Jan 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working harness and prompt bank for onboarding models for code refactor tasks where correctness is measured by: successful compilation, unit-test pass rate, and a lightweight style/regression scoring metric. Target audience: applied-ml engineers preparing prompt-based evaluation runners and SRE/cicd teams integrating the harness into nightly regression pipelines.

Scope:
- Domain: Python and a small subset of TypeScript refactors and code synthesis for helper functions.
- Tasks include: mechanical refactors (rename, extract method), behavior-preserving transforms, and constrained synthesis (style + tests passing).
- Evaluation axes: compile (yes/no), unit tests (pass rate), semantic correctness (fuzzed assertions), style constraints (PEP8 and project lint rules), and hallucination detection (unrelated imports, external network calls).

Quick summary of the harness design:
- Prompt bank (below) contains generation and refactor prompts with explicit constraints: required tests to pass, forbidden APIs, and allowed libs.
- Runner executes model -> captures artifact -> runs static checks -> executes unit tests in sandboxed container -> computes composite score.
- Regression detection: new model is flagged if composite score drops by >3 points absolute or unit-test pass rate drops by >5% vs baseline.

Prompt templates (standardized):
1) Refactor prompt (extract method):
"""
Task: Extract a helper function keeping behavior identical.
Requirements:
- New helper function must be pure (no global state).
- Add type annotations.
- All existing tests must still pass.
- Follow project style: max line length 100, snake_case names.
- Provide a short justification comment (1-2 sentences).

Input file: <CODE_SNIPPET>
Output: Return the full updated file content only (no explanation).
"""

2) Constrained synthesis prompt (implement function with tests):
"""
Task: Implement the function named `compute_eligibility` according to docstring.
Requirements:
- Must compile under Python 3.10.
- Must pass the provided pytest tests.
- No use of third-party packages other than `datetime` and `re` unless explicitly allowed.
- Add inline type hints and one-line docstring update if needed.

Input: <FILE_WITH_PLACEHOLDER_IMPLEMENTATION> and <TEST_FILE>
Output: Full updated file content only.
"""

3) Style-only constraint prompt (rename and normalize):
"""
Task: Normalize variable names to snake_case and format with black (line length 100).
Requirements:
- Do not change algorithmic logic.
- Add a brief comment at top: "# style-normalized by regen harness"

Input: <CODE_SNIPPET>
Output: Updated file content.
"""

Task bank (example tasks included in runner):
- T1: extract-calc-discount.py -> extract helper from a 120-line checkout calculation; has flaky float rounding tests.
  - Goal: refactor while making tests deterministic (hint: use Decimal).
  - Tests: tests/test_discount.py (4 asserts).

- T2: implement-eligibility.py -> placeholder for membership eligibility rules with edge-case tests (timestamps).
  - Goal: implement function to satisfy 6 tests including timezone edge.

- T3: rename-constants.ts -> TypeScript file with MANY constants in camelCase -> convert to UPPER_SNAKE and update exports.
  - Goal: compile with tsc and run a small jest suite.

- T4: simplify-graph-algo.py -> small refactor to clarify BFS code; preserve performance characteristics.
  - Goal: ensure all tests pass and no additional external imports.

- T5: security-sanitize.py -> remove direct subprocess calls replaced with subprocess.run with check and no shell=True.
  - Goal: ensure tests that assert no shell usage pass and lint warns resolved.

Unit tests and compile harness notes:
- Runner will create an isolated venv (Python 3.10), install only pytest and test-related helpers (no internet), and run `pytest -q` with timeout per test 5s.
- For TypeScript tasks we use node 18 and `npm ci` in an offline mirror; run `tsc --noEmit` then `npm test`.
- Sandboxing enforced with docker user namespaces and resource limits (config in linked artifact).

Scoring rubric (composite score out of 100):
- Compilation & safety checks: 30 points (compiles + no banned APIs = full 30).
- Unit tests: 40 points (normalized to pass rate).
- Style & lint: 20 points (pep8 / eslint; partial credit).
- Explanation hygiene: 10 points (presence of short justification comment and not returning extraneous text).

Regression detection logic:
- Baseline model: `redwood-refactor-v2` score logged as baseline per task.
- New model flagged if: composite score delta <= -3 OR unit-test pass rate delta <= -5%.
- We also look for new types of failures: new security findings or network calls introduced by generated code (immediate fail).

Example run output (ASCII table produced by harness):
+------+-----------------------------+--------+---------+-------+-----+
| Task | Model                       | Comp   | UT%     | Style | Score |
+------+-----------------------------+--------+---------+-------+-----+
| T1   | redwood-refactor-v2         | yes    | 100     | 18/20 | 98  |
| T1   | redwood-new-variant         | yes    | 75      | 16/20 | 83  |
| T2   | redwood-refactor-v2         | yes    | 100     | 20/20 | 100 |
| T2   | redwood-new-variant         | yes    | 50      | 18/20 | 78  |
+------+-----------------------------+--------+---------+-------+-----+

Note: if model outputs extra prose the harness will strip anything outside the code fence; if we detect missing code fences we mark as deduction in explanation hygiene.

Observed results (initial cold-run with `redwood-new-variant` on 2026-01-30):
- Overall composite drop vs baseline: -9.2 points. Main regression: T2 unit tests failing on timezone edge cases (flaky parsing).
- Action taken: temporary rollback to redwood-refactor-v2 for nightly regressions; added focused prompt variants for timezone handling.

Change log of prompt bank and runner decisions:
- 2026-01-10: initial draft of prompt templates and 5 tasks (this doc).
- 2026-01-18: added sandboxing rules and style scoring.
- 2026-01-30: ran initial model `redwood-new-variant`, captured regression on T2.
- 2026-02-03: added explicit requirement forbidding `dateutil` use in prompts and allowed only `datetime`/`zoneinfo`.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add a fuzzing stage for semantics beyond unit tests (property-based tests)? Pros/cons and compute cost.
- Determine thresholds per-customer: enterprise customers might require 100% UT pass to ship. Add config option.
- Integrate style auto-fix step (black/ruff) as an optional post-process to avoid penalizing minor formatting.
- Add more TypeScript tasks to better evaluate cross-language refactors.

Runner commands (developer quickstart):
- spin up local docker harness: ./scripts/dev_harness up --task T1 --model redwood-new-variant
- inspect artifacts: ./scripts/dev_harness artifacts --run-id <id>
- rerun only failing tests: ./scripts/dev_harness rerun --run-id <id> --task T2

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally verbose and includes TODOs and loose edges. Please comment in-line on the Confluence page CONFLUENCE-ENG-7821 and link PRs here when you adjust prompts or add tasks.
- If you add tasks, include a minimal test suite (pytest or jest) and an offline dependency manifest for deterministic runs.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Patel (eng-applied-ml)
